title: Decal-based blast scorch + bomber footstep marks — engine decal module + Kaboom Crew consumer (from Three.js webgl_decals)
intent: Per `docs/game-design/threejs-references-analysis.md §5.1`. Three.js `webgl_decals.html` shows how to project a small mesh onto existing geometry. We adopt the technique for: (a) BLAST SCORCH MARKS — after a BlastTile despawns, a darker decal stays on the floor for ~3 seconds before fading; (b) FOOTSTEP MARKS — light scuff decals behind walking bombers, persistent until the cell is destroyed or until ~30s elapse. Result: the arena visibly accumulates history. Repeated bombings in the same area darken the ground; bomber paths become visible. Modest implementation, strong arcade-history feel. Engine module under `engine/render/decals/` for reusability across any project.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/threejs-references-analysis.md §5.1` (Three.js decal example pattern). Builds on Three.js' `DecalGeometry` from three/examples/jsm/geometries/. Engine-first per CLAUDE.md (any AGF grid game with floors benefits — Kaboom now, future RPG/sample later). Pairs naturally with variable cell height (GDP-2026-05-28-010) — decals project onto cuboid top faces. Marked `could` because the floor already looks fine post-Wang autotile (GDP-002 + GDP-012); decals are arcade-history polish on top.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: ideally after Wang autotile (GDP-2026-05-28-002) + variable height (GDP-2026-05-28-010) ship, so decal projection has the final floor geometry to project onto.
READ FIRST: Three.js `webgl_decals.html` source + `three/examples/jsm/geometries/DecalGeometry.js` for the projection API.
DIRECTORY: NEW `engine/render/decals/`.
SCHEMA FILES (under `schemas/components/`):

decal.schema.json — Decal component { sourceMeshKey: string, position: [x,y,z], normal: [x,y,z], size: [w,h,d], color: '#hex', emissive?: '#hex', opacity?: number, lifetimeMs?: number, fadeStartMs?: number }
decal-spawn-request.schema.json — DecalSpawnRequest (transient — consumed same tick) { templateKey: string, position: [x,y,z], normal: [x,y,z], color?: '#hex' }
DECAL TEMPLATE REGISTRY (engine/render/decals/template-registry.ts):
registerDecalTemplate(key: string, template: DecalTemplate): void
DecalTemplate { defaultSize: [w,h,d], defaultColor: '#hex', defaultLifetimeMs: number, materialOverrides?: MaterialPatch }
Projects register decal templates at bootstrap (e.g. 'blast-scorch', 'footstep').
DECAL SPAWN SYSTEM (engine/render/decals/spawn-system.ts):
Consumes DecalSpawnRequest. Looks up template + creates a DecalGeometry on the target surface mesh:
Use Three.js DecalGeometry constructor: new DecalGeometry(targetMesh, position, orientation, size).
Position derived from request.position; orientation from a quaternion oriented to request.normal (project onto floor = normal pointing up).
Create a Mesh with the decal material + add as child entity of the target's cell.
Write Decal component with lifetimeMs + fadeStartMs.
Delete DecalSpawnRequest.
DECAL LIFETIME SYSTEM (engine/render/decals/lifetime-system.ts):
Per fixedUpdate: for each Decal entity, decrement lifetimeMs.
When lifetimeMs <= fadeStartMs (default fadeStartMs = 500ms before end): start opacity tween from 1.0 → 0.0.
When lifetimeMs <= 0: despawn the decal entity + dispose the DecalGeometry (Three.js doesn't auto-GC merged geometries).
INTEGRATION WITH VARIABLE HEIGHT (GDP-2026-05-28-010):
Decals project onto cell top faces. Position.y = cell.height (top face of cuboid).
Decals don't currently project onto cliff face sides — only top faces. (Future polish: cliff-face decals.)
FIRST CONSUMER 1 — BLAST SCORCH (examples/kaboom-crew):
Register a 'blast-scorch' template at bootstrap: { defaultSize: [1, 0.02, 1], defaultColor: '#1a0a05' (very dark warm), defaultLifetimeMs: 3000, fadeStartMs: 2500 }.
After BlastTile entity despawns (existing lifetime-system in blast-tile-lifetime-system.ts), spawn a DecalSpawnRequest at the cell's centre + Y = cell.height + normal = (0, 1, 0).
Result: blast cells leave a fading dark spot.
Multiple blasts on the same cell: decals stack (multiple Decal entities, each fades independently). Cell looks DARKER while multiple are active.
FIRST CONSUMER 2 — FOOTSTEP MARKS (examples/kaboom-crew):
Register a 'footstep' template: { defaultSize: [0.15, 0.02, 0.15], defaultColor: '#3a2a1a' (subtle dark scuff), defaultLifetimeMs: 30000, fadeStartMs: 27000 }.

Bomber walk-cycle (post-S104): when a leg's down-phase lands during the walk animation (existing footstep VFX from visual-style.md §6.2), spawn a DecalSpawnRequest at the bomber's current foot world position.
Alternating L/R per step. Result: bombers leave a trail of subtle dark scuffs that slowly fade.
Decals despawn early if the cell is destroyed (e.g. soft block destroyed under a footstep — decal disposed alongside).
PERFORMANCE BUDGET:
Decals per scene: ~50 at peak (multi-bomber + chains). Each DecalGeometry is a small Mesh (~100 vertices). Total ~5000 extra vertices. Negligible.
Periodic disposal of expired decals — pool / GC managed by the lifetime system.

Per visual-style.md §6.3 'No more than 2 simultaneous VFX layers on a single cell': blast scorch + blast-flash + particle burst would be 3. Document the cap — drop the SCORCH decal if blast-flash + particle burst both still active on the cell. Or extend the cap to 3 layers for the scorch case (it's a different kind — fading, not active).
MULTIPLAYER: each client runs its own decal sim. No protocol changes. Visual divergence per tab acceptable.
DETERMINISM: decal positions deterministic per blast event + footstep event. Bot-vs-bot regression unaffected (decals are visual).
DOCTOR INTEGRATION: engine doctor section 'Decals: N active, M templates registered'. Warning when N > 200 (potential leak).
UNIT TESTS:
Decal template registered + lookupable.
DecalSpawnRequest spawns a Decal entity at the requested position with the template's defaults.
Lifetime: decal fades opacity in last 500ms then despawns.
Cell destruction triggers despawn of decals on that cell.
Per-template tuning (size, lifetime, color) applied correctly.
VISUAL QA:
Blast at cell A → cell A's top face darkens for 3s then fades.
Bomber walks a 5-cell path → visible dark scuff trail behind, slowly fading over 30s.
Two bombers walk crossing paths → both trails visible.
Chain reaction → multiple darkening spots, eventual cell looks heavily-bombed.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Cliff-face decals (only top-face projection in v1).
Decal interaction with arena-theme palette (e.g. lab theme has lighter scorch). Default colours used universally.
Player-affected decal density (visual-only — no gameplay).
Decals on bomber meshes (e.g. damage scratch on bomber after a hit). Future polish.
Texture-based decal projection (e.g. an arrow texture). v1 is solid-color + emissive vertex masks.
Inter-decal blending (two decals at same position become a special MERGED decal). Stack visually.
